sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Detailed study guide and resources for Khilji Dynasty: Jalaluddin Khilji are currently being prepared. Check back soon for comprehensive explanations, summary diagrams, and expert preparation recommendations.

Key Dimensions of Study:

  • Definition, scope, and foundational theories.
  • Relevance to General Studies Paper & Contemporary contexts.
  • Core applications and structural framework.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the founder of the Khilji Dynasty in the Delhi Sultanate?
practiceQuestions.sol: Jalaluddin Firoz Khilji founded the Khilji dynasty in 1290 AD after overthrowing the last rulers of the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: In which year did Jalaluddin Firoz Khilji ascend the throne of Delhi?
practiceQuestions.sol: Jalaluddin Khilji became the Sultan of Delhi in 1290 AD, marking the end of the Mamluk dynasty and the beginning of the 'Khilji Revolution'. [Primary Reference: Standard Medieval History Canons - Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the original name or title of Jalaluddin before he became Sultan?
practiceQuestions.sol: Before ascending the throne, Jalaluddin was known as Malik Firoz, serving under the later Mamluk rulers. [Primary Reference: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi by Ziauddin Barani]

practiceQuestions.q: Which Mongol leader invaded India during the reign of Jalaluddin Khilji and later embraced Islam along with his followers?
opts: Abdullah (grandson of Halaku) / Ulugh and the New Muslims
practiceQuestions.sol: During Jalaluddin's reign, the Mongols led by Abdullah invaded. Later, thousands of Mongols under Ulugh settled near Delhi, came to be known as 'New Muslims', and Jalaluddin even gave his daughter in marriage to one of their leaders. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History / Medieval Histories]

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the nephew and son-in-law of Jalaluddin Khilji who eventually assassinated him?
practiceQuestions.sol: Alauddin Khilji was the nephew and son-in-law of Jalaluddin. He deceitfully assassinated Jalaluddin at Kara in 1296 AD to usurp the throne. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7 History]

practiceQuestions.q: Where was Jalaluddin Firoz Khilji assassinated by Alauddin Khilji?
practiceQuestions.sol: Jalaluddin was murdered by Alauddin at Kara (near modern Allahabad/Prayagraj) when he visited him unarmed to show affection. [Primary Reference: Comprehensive History of India - A.B. Habibullah]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the notable characteristic of Jalaluddin Khilji's domestic governance policy?
opts: Blood and Iron policy of extreme terror
Mildness and a benevolent, non-tyrannical approach
Forced conversion of all Hindus to Islam
Total decentralization of power to local Hindu chiefs

Jalaluddin believed that the state should be based on the willing support of the governed, earning him a reputation for mildness and reluctance to shed blood (hence called 'Clemency Jalaluddin'). [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the famous Sufi poet and scholar executed or punished during Jalaluddin's reign for seditious remarks?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sidi Maula, a foreign dervish, was executed under charges of plotting against the Sultan, an act that shocked contemporary public opinion due to its severity. [Primary Reference: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi]

practiceQuestions.q: Which important fortress expedition of Jalaluddin Khilji was abandoned due to his reluctance to sacrifice Muslim lives?
practiceQuestions.sol: When Jalaluddin besieged Ranthambore (1290-91), he realized the fort was too strong and retreated, famously stating that he would not value a hundred forts above the hair of a single Muslim. [Primary Reference: NCERT & Medieval Sources]

practiceQuestions.q: Who held the office of the 'Ariz-i-Mumalik' (Minister of War) initially under Jalaluddin Khilji?
practiceQuestions.sol: Before becoming Sultan, Alauddin Khilji was appointed as the Ariz-i-Mumalik (Minister of War) by Jalaluddin Khilji, which gave him command over the military apparatus. [Primary Reference: Delhi Sultanate Administrative History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the rise of the Khilji dynasty under Jalaluddin mark a fundamental shift in the character of the Delhi Sultanate compared to the Mamluk (Slave) dynasty?
opts: It ended the monopoly of high offices by a narrow racial/tribal Turkish aristocracy, opening them to broader Indo-Muslim nobility.
It replaced Islam with a secular state ideology.
It abolished the Iqta system completely and introduced cash salaries for all.
It shifted the capital permanently from Delhi to Lahore.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Khilji revolution ended the rigid ethnic exclusivity of the Turkish ruling class, allowing non-Turks and Indian Muslims to attain high administrative positions, thus broadening the social base of the Sultanate. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India: From Sultanat to the Mughals]

practiceQuestions.q: What was Jalaluddin Khilji's fundamental rationale behind his policy of clemency towards political opponents and rebels?
opts: Extreme weakness and fear of military retaliation by provincial governors.
A philosophical belief that a Muslim kingdom in India could not be established through unmitigated terror alone and needed moral consensus.
Direct orders from the Caliph in Baghdad.
A secret pact with the Mongol invaders to share imperial taxes.
practiceQuestions.sol: Jalaluddin was pragmatic and realized that the Sultanate was too expansive to be ruled solely by Balban's 'blood and iron'. He believed ruling an indigenous majority required a degree of compromise and popular acceptance. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Jalaluddin Khilji handle Malik Chajju's rebellion in Kara?
opts: He executed Malik Chajju and his entire family publicly.
He pardoned him and treated him with leniency, much to the anger of his hardline commanders.
He banished him permanently to Central Asia.
He converted Malik Chajju's jagir into a crown territory.
practiceQuestions.sol: When Malik Chajju (a nephew of Balban) revolted, Jalaluddin defeated him but pardoned him, releasing his captured nobles and refusing harsh punishments. This caused Ahmad Chap and other officers to criticize his lack of firmness. [Primary Reference: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi]

practiceQuestions.q: The arrival and settlement of 'New Muslims' in Delhi during Jalaluddin's reign had what long-term implication for the Sultanate?
opts: They became the most loyal standing army for Alauddin Khilji's conquests.
They periodically posed security challenges and integration issues, leading to severe repression later.
They introduced democratic principles into the Turkish administration.
They completely replaced the Turkish nobility within two years.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Mongol converts ('New Muslims') settled near Delhi. While Jalaluddin welcomed them, their cultural differences, economic tensions, and suspected conspiracies later created internal security concerns for Alauddin Khilji. [Primary Reference: Medieval Indian History Textbooks]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of Jalaluddin Khilji's military campaign into Malwa (specifically Mandu)?
opts: It permanently annexed Malwa and Gujarat to the Delhi Sultanate in one stroke.
It served as a limited punitive raid rather than a full-scale annexation, showcasing his reluctance for aggressive imperial expansion.
It was a total military disaster resulting in the capture of Jalaluddin.
It established a permanent trade treaty with the Yadavas of Devagiri.
practiceQuestions.sol: Jalaluddin captured Mandu in Malwa, but when his officers suggested marching further for deep southern conquests, he declined, demonstrating that his vision lacked the aggressive expansionism later seen under Alauddin. [Primary Reference: Comprehensive History of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did Ziauddin Barani and orthodox contemporary chroniclers criticize Jalaluddin Khilji's lenient treatment of Hindus and rebels?
opts: Because they believed a Sultan must rule with awe, fear, and strict Islamic supremacy without compromise.
Because Jalaluddin had abolished all taxes on non-Muslims entirely.
Because he converted the royal court into a Hindu religious center.
Because he handed over Delhi's administration to Mongol refugees.
practiceQuestions.sol: Chroniclers like Barani expected the Sultan to enforce strict subordination of non-Muslims and merciless punishment for rebels (the Balbanian model). Jalaluddin's refusal to do so was viewed by them as a sign of weakness ('weak-kneed policy'). [Primary Reference: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi by Barani]

practiceQuestions.q: What role did Alauddin Khilji play prior to his uncle's assassination that indirectly prepared him for capturing power?
opts: He led a successful and immensely profitable raid on Devagiri (Deogiri), accumulating vast wealth.
He successfully repelled the major Mongol invasion single-handedly.
He served as the Prime Minister and controlled the treasury directly.
He organized a democratic election among Turkish nobles.
practiceQuestions.sol: Alauddin raided Devagiri in 1296 without Jalaluddin's prior formal permission, acquiring immense gold and silver. This independent financial resource gave him the military backing and independence needed to stage his coup. [Primary Reference: NCERT History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Jalaluddin Khilji react when he learned about Alauddin's unauthorized and massive wealth collection from Devagiri?
opts: He immediately dispatched an army to arrest Alauddin and confiscate all treasures.
He reacted with paternal affection, foolishly walking into Alauddin's trap at Kara to personally collect the wealth.
He rewarded Alauddin by appointing him Crown Prince publicly in Delhi.
He fled to Gujarat fearing a rebellion.
practiceQuestions.sol: Instead of taking military precautions against his ambitious nephew, Jalaluddin trusted him blindly, visited Kara unprotected to meet him, and was killed. [Primary Reference: Medieval Chronicles]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the administrative status of Delhi during the transition from the Mamluks to the Khiljis under Jalaluddin?
opts: The capital was temporarily shifted to Kilokhari (Qilugarh) by Jalaluddin.
Delhi was completely razed to the ground and rebuilt.
The capital was moved to Devagiri immediately.
Delhi was divided into four autonomous administrative zones.
practiceQuestions.sol: Jalaluddin initially held his court and resided at Kilokhari (built by Kaiqubad) rather than entering the old city of Delhi right away, symbolizing a fresh beginning for the new dynasty. [Primary Reference: Architectural & Historical Survey of Delhi]

practiceQuestions.q: Which statement best captures the historical legacy of Jalaluddin Khilji's brief six-year reign (1290–1296)?
opts: It was a golden age of architectural marvels and economic reforms.
It served as a transitional, liberal interlude that broke aristocratic rigidity, paving the way for the robust imperial expansion of Alauddin.
It permanently established a parliamentary system in the Delhi Sultanate.
It witnessed the complete destruction of Delhi by Mongol armies.
practiceQuestions.sol: Jalaluddin's reign bridged the gap between the autocratic, exclusive Mamluk regime and the aggressive militarism of Alauddin, marking the end of strict racial exclusivity in high offices. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Jalaluddin Firoz Khilji:
1. He was the first ruler of the Delhi Sultanate to put forward the view that the state should be based on the willing support of the governed.
2. He ruthlessly suppressed all political opponents and rebels using the policy of 'blood and iron'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Jalaluddin openly stated that since a large majority of the people in India were Hindus and did not follow true religion, a Muslim king could not rule with extreme tyranny. Statement 2 is incorrect because Jalaluddin was famously known for his policy of clemency, not 'blood and iron' (which was Balban's policy). [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'New Muslims' during the reign of Jalaluddin Khilji:
1. They were Mongol invaders who accepted Islam and were settled near Delhi by the Sultan.
2. They were given high administrative posts and allotted extensive jagirs, which instantly pleased the orthodox Turkish nobles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Around 4,000 Mongols under Ulugh converted to Islam and settled near Delhi ('New Muslims'). Statement 2 is incorrect because the orthodox Turkish nobles were actually displeased and suspicious of these recent converts being integrated into the nobility and given residential quarters near the capital. [Primary Reference: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the conspiracy against Jalaluddin Khilji:
1. Sidi Maula, a Sufi dervish, was executed under suspicion of being involved in a conspiracy to assassinate Jalaluddin and place a rival prince on the throne.
2. The harsh execution of Sidi Maula received universal praise from all contemporary chroniclers and common people without any backlash.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Sidi Maula was accused of plotting with disgruntled nobles against Jalaluddin and was executed. Statement 2 is incorrect because his brutal execution caused widespread public grief and fear, and people believed that divine retribution (a severe dust storm and famine) followed this unjust act. [Primary Reference: Ziauddin Barani]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Jalaluddin's military actions:
1. He successfully captured the Ranthambore fort after a prolonged and brutal multi-year siege.
2. He led an expedition to Ranthambore, but withdrew because he did not want to sacrifice Muslim lives to capture a stone fort.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Jalaluddin failed to capture Ranthambore. Statement 2 is correct: when his officers urged continuing the siege, he refused, uttering his famous remark that he did not value a hundred forts above the hair of a single Muslim. [Primary Reference: NCERT History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the transition of power from Jalaluddin to Alauddin:
1. Alauddin invited Jalaluddin to Kara unarmed under the pretext of handing over the enormous wealth plundered from Devagiri.
2. Jalaluddin was assassinated while performing prayers on the banks of the Yamuna/Ganges at Kara in 1296 AD.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements 1 and 2 are correct. Alauddin lured Jalaluddin to Kara by promising to present the Devagiri loot. When the trusting Sultan arrived with only a few attendants and bent forward to embrace Alauddin, assassins attacked and beheaded him near the river bank in 1296 AD. [Primary Reference: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the administrative background of Jalaluddin Khilji:
1. Before becoming Sultan, he had served as an officer and governor under the Mamluk sultans, including Balban and Kaiqubad.
2. He belonged to the pure, high-born Turkish elite stock that had dominated the Delhi Sultanate since its inception.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Jalaluddin had a long military career serving Mamluk rulers. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Khiljis were ethnically distinct from the pure-bred Turks; they were of Afghan/Turco-Afghan descent or mixed stock, which is why the old Turkish nobility initially looked down upon them as parvenus. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Jalaluddin's handling of external threats:
1. He successfully repelled a major invasion by the Mongol leader Abdullah, defeating them on the frontiers of Delhi.
2. He never encountered any Mongol incursions during his reign due to a permanent peace treaty signed with Hulagu Khan's successors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: When Abdullah invaded with a vast Mongol host, Jalaluddin marched out, engaged them near the borders, and forced a retreat, after which many Mongols settled in India. Statement 2 is incorrect because Mongol incursions did occur (such as Abdullah's invasion), and no permanent peace treaty existed. [Primary Reference: Comprehensive History of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ahmad Chap, a prominent officer under Jalaluddin Khilji:
1. He was a close military commander who consistently urged the Sultan to adopt a strong, stern policy against rebels and political rivals.
2. He supported Jalaluddin's policy of total forgiveness and soft governance towards Malik Chajju and other conspirators.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Ahmad Chap represented the hardline faction among the Khilji nobility, frequently warning Jalaluddin that his leniency would embolden enemies. Statement 2 is incorrect because Ahmad Chap vehemently opposed the pardoning of Malik Chajju and other rebels. [Primary Reference: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the economic and social conditions during Jalaluddin's brief reign:
1. Wine drinking and public assemblies of nobles were strictly banned and effectively eradicated throughout his rule.
2. Despite his personal piety and mild nature, wine drinking and gatherings were widely prevalent among the nobility, and he chose to overlook them rather than enforce prohibition harshly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because total prohibition and strict wine bans were enacted later under Alauddin Khilji, not Jalaluddin. Statement 2 is correct: Jalaluddin was personally aware of wine parties and political plotting taking place at gatherings (where even conspiracies against him were discussed), but due to his tolerant and soft disposition, he gave mild warnings instead of harsh punishments. [Primary Reference: Ziauddin Barani]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the historical assessment of Jalaluddin Khilji:
1. Contemporary chroniclers unanimously lauded him as the greatest conqueror in Islamic history.
2. Modern historians view him as a humanitarian ruler whose lack of political ruthlessness ultimately led to his tragic downfall and opened the path for imperial consolidation under his successor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because contemporary orthodox chroniclers like Barani criticized him for lacking royal sternness and political terror. Statement 2 is correct: modern historians evaluate him as a mild, benevolent ruler whose humane reluctance to shed blood made him vulnerable, culminating in his assassination by Alauddin, who then used that wealth to build a centralized empire. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]
